children: Malaysian palm oil futures edged higher on Friday, underpinned by firmer rival Dalian soyoil prices, and were on track for a small weekly gain.

The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained 10 ringgit, or 0.2%, to 4,914 ringgit ($1,215.43) a metric ton by the midday break. The contract has risen 0.35% so far this week.
Crude palm oil futures traded higher, tracking stronger Dalian soybean oil prices, said David Ng, a proprietary trader at Kuala Lumpur-based trading firm Iceberg X Sdn Bhd.
"We see support at 4,900 ringgit and resistance at 5,080 ringgit," he said.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.07%, while its palm oil contract
shed 0.17%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were down 0.31%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
Malaysia's palm oil inventories likely rose to a seven-month high in August, driven by the strongest production in nine months and a decline in exports, a Reuters survey showed.
Oil prices rose, heading for their steepest weekly gain since mid-July, as rising tension and renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities heightened concerns over Middle East supply risks. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Indonesian state-owned plantation company Agrinas Palma Nusantara is targeting palm oil output of 1.5 million tons next year, said Chief Executive Mohammad Abdul Ghani.

Indonesia's effort to exert control over global prices for its vast natural resources by setting up a new commodities exchange will struggle to compete with established bourses and risks backfiring if participation is mandatory.
Palm oil may retrace further to 4,850 ringgit per ton, as suggested by a rising trendline and a retracement analysis, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.
